hints: Every vertex must have equal incoming and outgoing degree for a closed Euler tour to use all edges.
Hierholzer's algorithm follows unused edges until trapped, then inserts those subroutes into the tour.
Start at city 1 and verify the resulting tour contains exactly m edges.
analogy: Walk every unused mail road once, stitching closed loops together whenever a route branches.
example: A triangle has a closed route 1-2-3-1 using all three roads.
algorithm: Check degree balance, then run iterative Hierholzer using adjacency stacks and a vertex stack. Reverse the popped circuit and ensure its length is m+1.
correctness: Balanced degrees plus the constructed circuit using every edge proves a valid Euler tour; checking length catches disconnected edge components.
